Houston Stewart Chamberlain ( / ˈ tʃ eɪ m b ər l ɪ n / ; 9 September 1855 – 9 January 1927) was a British-German-French philosopher who wrote works about political philosophy and natural science . His writing promoted German ethnonationalism , antisemitism , scientific racism , and Nordicism ; he has been described as a "racialist writer". [ 1 ] His best-known book, the two-volume Die Grundlagen des neunzehnten Jahrhunderts ( The Foundations of the Nineteenth Century ), [ 2 ] published in 1899, became highly influential in the pan-Germanic Völkisch movements of the early 20th century, and later influenced the antisemitism of Nazi racial policy . In the early 1920s, Chamberlain met and encouraged Adolf Hitler : he has been referred to as "Hitler's John the Baptist ". [ 3 ]
